story.title: The Water Cycle
paragraphs_en: A lonely cloud was floating all alone in the sky. It looked sad. Suddenly, a gust of wind came from behind, forcing the cloud to float even further. The wind asked him, “Why do you look so sad, Mr. Cloud, everything alright with you?” “No, my dear,” said the cloud, “I am not all happy. I don’t have enough water in me. How will I show my face to the farmers in the villages who are waiting for rain for their crops. And how will I meet the little kids in towns and cities who want relief from the scorching heat? There is almost no water in me.” “Why is there no water in you, Mr. Cloud?” asked a little bird that was flying in the air when she overheard the conversation between the wind and the cloud.

“Ah, little bird. Want to know everything, don’t you? The water cycle has been disturbed this year.” “What is the water cycle?” asked the little bird. “The water cycle manages the flow of water in nature . Water evaporates from water bodies and forms water vapour. This water vapour reaches the sky and turns into tiny water droplets. These water droplets then, form clouds like me. Due to too many droplets, the cloud becomes heavy and discharges the water, this water again reaches back to the water bodies. Then the cycle starts again. When there are too few droplets, the cloud is unable to provide any rain to anyone. That is the situation with me,” replied the cloud.

“This year has been particularly bad. Human beings have been using water so rapidly that there is very less water in all the water bodies,” said the wind. The little bird felt very bad for the cloud. When it grew dark, she flew back home. She narrated what the cloud and the wind said to her mamma and papa. They felt very bad for the cloud. The next day, when mamma and papa bird went to work, the little bird decided to go to the countryside and speak to the people there. she flew and flew till she reached the countryside. There were some milkmaids resting under a tree. “Hi, everyone!” said the little bird. The milkmaids seemed to be surprised on seeing her. “Hello, little bird! Do you wish to speak to us?”

“Yes, I indeed wish to. I wish to discuss how the water levels in streams, ponds and lakes are so low. Do you know that the water cycle is disturbed because of this? Clouds do not contain enough water to provide rain.” replied the bird. “Yes, we know that. But what can we do? The water bodies will only be revived after it rains,” answered a milkmaid. “But we can’t wait till it rains heavily. Besides, it will not rain heavily until evaporation takes place. And large-scale evaporation cannot take place until there is enough water in the water bodies,“ the little bird said, explaining the basic principles of the water cycle.

If it doesn’t rain then neither us nor you will have enough water for household chores or even drinking,” explained the little bird further, “do you want to get into such a situation?” “I understand. This is so sad,” said one milkmaid. “We must do something,” said another. “But what can we do?” commented the third. “We must start saving water bit by bit and channelize it to our lakes and ponds,” said the first milkmaid. “If we want to save water bit by bit, we must try rooftop rainwater harvesting. I googled it last night. It is very simple and cost-effective.

Whenever it rains, the rainwater slides from the roof to collect the water. A storage tank is installed in the ground to collect the rainwater. It may sound expensive, but it is actually not. If we try, we can arrange for a makeshift rooftop rainwater harvesting system.” “But we are poor people. We don’t have any savings as such, so how can we manage to build such infrastructure on our own?” asked the first milkmaid. “In that case, we should run a fundraising campaign. We can go from door to door asking for funds and run a campaign on social media as well. From the funds collected, we can easily buy the required materials,” said the second milkmaid.

“This is a good idea,” everyone agreed. From the very next day, they began implementing their plan. As soon as they received the funds, they installed one rooftop rainwater harvesting system. Within a year, most homes had a rooftop rainwater harvesting system. Both animals and humans contributed to these funds and learnt to live in complete harmony. They also started experimenting with other kinds of water conservation systems like reviving old stepwells and creating new drains and dams to store water.

“In that case, we should run a fundraising campaign.
We can go from door to door asking for funds and run a campaign on social media as well.
From the funds collected, we can easily buy the required materials,” said the second milkmaid.
“This is a good idea,” everyone agreed.
From the very next day, they began implementing their plan.
As soon as they received the funds, they installed one rooftop rainwater harvesting system.
Within a year, most homes had a rooftop rainwater harvesting system.
Both animals and humans contributed to these funds and learnt to live in complete harmony.
They also started experimenting with other kinds of water conservation systems like reviving old stepwells and creating new drains and dams to store water.
